title: Chicken Parmesan
description:
As our friend Grace Pilato says “This is a dish that everyone loves – it is so dependable, inexpensive, and deliciously appetizing, and the presentation works beautifully.” We’re basing this recipe on her book “Cooking With Grace.”
I first had this at Linda’s Grand-mother’s in New York, where we were living after graduating from college. In her 80’s and living in a fourth -floor walk-up, Nani would often make this for us when we came to visit. She usually made it with veal (but chicken is just as good), and sometimes would also make homemade pasta, bread and vinegar peppers, and, of course, her own pasta sauce.
Her apartment always smelled so wonderful when we arrived, especially the scent of garlic cooking in the hot olive oil as she made the cutlets. We think of those great visits every time we make this.
This dish can also be made with veal or flattened pork tenderloin. Without the marinara and cheese, this becomes Chicken Cutlets or Chicken Milanese, and the Vinegar Peppers are a magical accompaniment.
ingredients: 6 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves (always make extra!)
½ cup Parmesan cheese, grated (or Locatelli mixed in)
2 cups or more Italian breadcrumbs (or fresh crumbs with spices)
6 tablespoons olive oil or oil and butter combination
1 cup Marinara Sauce or other tomato sauce
Vinegar Pepper Recipe Follows (If using, you should make the peppers first.)
directions: Clean the chicken breasts of the scrappy filets and extra fat, cartilage, or connecting tissues. (You can make some chicken stock with all the leftover little pieces.)
Slice thick cutlets horizontally (maybe after firming them up in a freezer for a few minutes).

Another technique for the thicker cutlets – butterflying – also starts by slicing horizontally in half, but stopping ¼ inch before the side end. Open the cutlet like a book and flatten a little with you hand.
With the chicken pieces skin side down and between two sheets of plastic wrap or parchment paper, pound to ¼ - ½ inch even thickness. This also helps to tenderize them.
If the flattened pieces are bigger than the main part of your hand, cut them in half (unless you really want the cutlets to fill most of the plate).
Season with a little salt and pepper.

These are so good by themselves, but they are an especially tasty complement to the “friedness” of the Chicken Cutlets. If we have these peppers and sauce, I usually leave the Marinara and cheese off the cutlets.
ACTIVE TIME: 15 MIN
START TO FINISH: 1 ½ HOURS
Vinegar Peppers
Put the blackened peppers in a plastic container or bag and tightly seal for about 10 minutes.
At this point, you should be able to fairly easily remove and discard the skins.
1-2 garlic cloves, peeled
4 peppers, red, yellow or orange
¼ cup extra virgin olive oil
¾ cup good balsamic vinegar
Cut the tops off the peppers and cut down the sides along the ribs.
Clean out the seeds and trim back all the white of the ribs on the inside.
With skin side up, flatten with the palm of you hand so that the lay fairly flat.

Place on a cookie sheet pan and broil on the top shelf of the oven until the skins are charred and blackened, about 15 minutes. Rotate the pan occasionally during the broiling to make sure all are charred.

Arrange three bowls for breading the cutlets: one with the flour; the second with the eggs, milk or water, and cheese, all well blended; and the third with the bread crumbs, sprinkled with garlic salt (if desired).

Dredge the seasoned chicken breasts one at a time in the flour. Then dip each floured piece of chicken in the egg and cheese mixture, shaking off any excess, and place in another bowl. Finally, place each breast in the bread crumb mixture and press with your fingers to coat both sides well. Place on rack.
Heat 2-3 tablespoons of the oil (or oil and butter mixture) in a large pan. Add the smashed garlic cloves (and enjoy the smell!)
When the oil is hot, add the cutlets without crowding, maybe 3-4 at a time, depending on the pan size. They should sizzle.
Cook for about 2 minutes, until nicely browned, turn and cook the other side similarly. Remove from the pan and place on cookie sheet with a rack.
Sprinkle each cutlet with a little Parmesan while hot. When all are ready, “paint” cutlets with a spoonful of the Marinara sauce and top with the slices of provolone.
Melt the cheese in the oven and serve!
Combine the oil and vinegar with a smashed garlic clove, and heat moderately for a minute or two.
Add the peppers, with a sprinkling of salt, and sir to coat well.
Allow the peppers to marinate for an hour, or longer if you have the time.
When serving, put a pepper slice or two and some of the vinegar sauce on the cutlets. Yum!
